judgments.reasoning_cat1: "securities or other assets" is a deliberately open definition of "Securities" and "unless otherwise agreed in writing" leaves the scope of the master agreement's governance elastic, but the operative mechanics are plain.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long enumerated definition with fixed triggers and a 15-day dismissal window; the terms "similar law" and "similar official" are catch-alls but are anchored by the specifics.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line cross-reference definition whose paragraph citation is garbled in this copy, but the referent (Paragraph 4(a)) is unmistakable from Paragraph 4(a) itself.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A purely arithmetic definition (percentage applied to Repurchase Price) with no evaluative word to construe.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A pure signpost definition pointing to Paragraph 3(b); nothing to construe.

judgments.reasoning_cat2: Income drives Paragraph 5, Paragraph 11(b)(ii) and Annex VI paragraph 9, and Annex I paragraph 3 overrides the Paragraph 5(ii) branch; those interactions are internally coherent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A signpost definition with no substantive content of its own.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "the price ... obtained from a generally recognized source agreed to by the parties or the most recent closing bid quotation from such a source" is genuinely ambiguous about which source governs, who chooses it, and what happens when no generally recognized source exists for illiquid mortgage paper; "unless contrary to market practice" adds a further open-ended escape.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It drives Paragraph 4(a) margin calls and sits against Paragraph 11(d)'s acknowledgment that all Securities trade in a recognized market and that the nondefaulting party may pick the source in its sole discretion — a real tension over who values the collateral.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A precise daily-accrual formula on a stated day-count basis with an express reduction for amounts already paid.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Fits Paragraph 2(r)'s Repurchase Price build-up and Annex VI's parallel Sell Back Differential; no inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One clause stating the rate is a per annum percentage; nothing evaluative.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An externally verifiable benchmark with a tie-breaker for multiple published rates.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line date definition; "are to be transferred" versus actually transferred is a slight looseness but hardly contestable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A mechanical adjustment formula tracking cash flows under Paragraphs 4(a), 4(b) and 5.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition expressly sweeps in Additional Purchased Securities and excludes returned Securities, leaving little to argue about on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Squares with Paragraph 4(a)/(b), Paragraph 9 substitution and Annex I's added Paragraph 9(c); no inconsistency located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Plainly defined and expressly extended to dates fixed under Paragraphs 3(c) and 11.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Demand must be made "no later than such time as is customary in accordance with market practice", an undefined external standard, and demand may be by telephone.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The mirror image of 4(a); "Market Value" and the bracketed netting adjustment carry the same interpretive softness, and "cash or Purchased Securities" at Buyer's option is loosely bounded.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Reads consistently with Paragraph 2(o) (Purchase Price adjustments) and Paragraph 2(p) (exclusion of returned Securities); no direct contradiction found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clear two-branch timing rule keyed to the Margin Notice Deadline, though "close of business in the relevant market" borrows an external referent.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Depends on the Paragraph 2(i) fallback to "market practice" and mirrors Annex V paragraph 2(e); consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short attribution rule that simply defers to later agreement, leaving no allocation default if the parties never agree — a gap more than an ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Paragraph 2(o) assumes cash transfers are attributable to particular Transactions for Purchase Price adjustment, so the absence of a default rule creates mild friction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A permissive threshold provision conditioned on prior agreement; the wording is self-limiting and clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Annex I contains no such agreed threshold, so the clause is simply dormant; no conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Another permissive election clause with an express calculation instruction; nothing vague.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Annex IV paragraph 4(b)(iii) and Annex VII paragraph 1(a) impose transaction- or fund-level margining in specified cases, which supplements rather than contradicts this election.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Buyer's choice between transferring Income and applying it, exercised "as Buyer shall reasonably determine in its discretion", plus the two carve-outs, gives a court a discretion standard to construe.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A three-option transfer mechanic with a reasonableness qualifier on requested documentation; concrete and workable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Annex III paragraph 2 and Annex VII paragraph 5 build on it consistently for international transfers and Fund custodians.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "To the extent required by applicable law" makes the segregation duty contingent on an external standard, and the free-rehypothecation sentence is broadly worded.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The disclosure is left with unresolved bracketed alternatives — "[will]* [may]**", "[its clearing bank]* [third parties]**" — so the text does not say which words apply, a mechanical defect on its face.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A deeming provision with a Market Value proviso; its clarity depends on the contestable Paragraph 2(j) valuation definition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It deems Buyer to have accepted substitution in seller-custody Transactions, whereas Annex I's new Paragraph 9(c) gives Buyer an express right to decline substitution and Annex I paragraph 2 makes the Annex govern — a genuine tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional list of representations with a deemed-repetition sentence; the terms are objective and verifiable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Annex I paragraph 5, Annex IV paragraph 1 and Annex VII paragraph 4 all add representations expressly "in addition to" Paragraph 10, so the scheme is consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The trigger list mixes strict-liability defaults with materiality and notice qualifiers, and item (iii) makes any failure to comply with Paragraph 4 an immediate default without cure, which invites argument about what compliance required.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is expanded by Annex III paragraph 8(a) and Annex V paragraph 4(a) and read through Annex IV paragraph 5; whether a disputed margin call under Paragraph 4(a) counts as a default is where the interaction bites.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Automatic deemed exercise on an Act of Insolvency coupled with a duty to give notice "as promptly as practicable" creates a soft timing standard, but the acceleration mechanic itself is definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is the trigger for 11(b)-(f), Annex V paragraph 4(b) and Annex III paragraph 8(b), all of which reference it consistently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Three concrete consequences stated in operative terms; "any other amounts owing hereunder" is a mild catch-all.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Works together with 11(d)(i) and 11(g), and Annex VI paragraph 11 rewrites "Repurchase Prices" here to include Sell Back Prices; no contradiction found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A deemed-transfer rule conditioned on tender of the aggregate Repurchase Prices; clear on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Complements 11(d)(ii) and 11(e)/(f); no conflicting provision located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "in a recognized market (or otherwise in a commercially reasonable manner)", "at such price or prices as the nondefaulting party may reasonably deem satisfactory", and the alternative of self-crediting at a price "obtained from a generally recognized source" are exactly the sort of open standards two parties read differently after a collateral liquidation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It has to be read with Paragraph 2(j) Market Value, with the following acknowledgment that all Securities trade in a recognized market, and with 11(g) damages; whether the nondefaulting party's chosen prices bind the defaulting party is the pinch point.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A blanket deeming that all Securities "are instruments traded in a recognized market" is a factual fiction whose reach over illiquid mortgage collateral is contestable, and it hands the nondefaulting party "sole discretion" to establish the pricing source.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It contradicts its own neighbouring text and Paragraph 11(d), which expressly contemplate that there may be no recognized market or generally recognized source, and it collides with the Paragraph 2(j) requirement of a source "agreed to by the parties".

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Damages measured by the excess of replacement cost over Repurchase Price, plus a broad tail ("or otherwise hereunder"); the drafting is one-directional but the measure is definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Addresses only the case where the defaulting party is Buyer, leaving the Seller-default measure to 11(d)(i) and 11(g); the asymmetry is deliberate and consistent with 11(f).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single-purpose cap keyed to a fixed determination date; the sentence is broken across a page footer in this copy but the meaning is recoverable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Caps the Repurchase Price used in 11(c) and 11(e) while Paragraph 2(r) has it accrue continuously — an express override rather than a conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-sentence cumulative-remedies saving clause; standard and unambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Reinforces rather than disturbs the remedies in 11(d)-(h) and Annex V paragraph 4(b).
